2607.01224.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
2607.01224.paper_summary: Memory expertise is a learned skill: knowing what to encode, when to retrieve, and how to organize knowledge--a capacity known in cognitive science as metamemory. We bring this perspective to LLMs by treating memory management as a trainable skill. We promote file-system operations to first-class memory actions alongside task actions, letting the model itself decide how to manage its memory. This memory skill improves along two axes: the structure that supports it (prompts, file schemas, action vocabulary), and the proficiency of the model exercising it. Both axes resist manual optimization: episodes in long-horizon tasks run for thousands of steps, and a single memory mistake can hide long before it surfaces, making human review of full trajectories impractical. We introduce AutoMem, a framework that automates both axes. In the first loop, a strong LLM reviews complete agent trajectories and iteratively revises the memory structure that shapes how the agent interacts with its memory files. In the second loop, the agent's own good memory decisions are identified from many episodes and used as training signal to sharpen the model's memory proficiency directly. Across three procedurally generated long-horizon games (Crafter, MiniHack, and NetHack), optimizing memory alone--without modifying the model's task-action behavior--improved the base agent's performance ~2x-4x, bringing a 32B open-weight model competitive with frontier systems such as Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Thinking. Our results show that memory management is an independently learnable skill, and a high-leverage objective yielding large gains on long-horizon tasks.
2607.01224.paper_summary_zh: 記憶專業是一種學習技能：知道什麼該編碼、何時檢索以及如何組織知識——這種能力在認知科學中被稱為元記憶。我們通過將記憶管理視為可訓練的技能，將這一觀點帶入LLM。我們將文件系統操作提升為一級記憶行動，與任務行動並列，讓模型自己決定如何管理其記憶。這項記憶技能在兩個軸向上改進：支持它的結構（提示、文件架構、行動詞彙）以及模型運用它的熟練度。這兩個軸向都抵抗手動優化：長期任務中的事件運行數千步，而單一的記憶錯誤可能在浮現之前隱藏很久，使得人類無法實際檢查完整的軌跡。我們引入了AutoMem，一個自動化這兩個軸向的框架。在第一個循環中，一個強大的LLM審查完整的代理軌跡，並迭代修訂塑造代理如何與其記憶文件互動的記憶結構。在第二個循環中，從許多事件中識別出代理自己的良好記憶決策，並用作訓練信號以直接提高模型的記憶熟練度。在三個程序生成的長期遊戲（Crafter、MiniHack和NetHack）中，僅優化記憶——而不修改模型的任務行動行為——使基礎代理的性能提高了約2倍至4倍，使一個32B開放權重模型在與Claude Opus 4.5和Gemini 3.1 Pro Thinking等前沿系統的競爭中具備了競爭力。我們的結果顯示，記憶管理是一項可以獨立學習的技能，並且是一個高杠杆的目標，能在長期任務中帶來巨大的收益。
